paper.title: Maternal education and child health: Causal evidence from Denmark
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement and no Statistics Denmark project reference is printed. …

registers.name_in_paper: administrative data on schooling and education (completed education from October 1973; ongoing education registered in October each year from 1981 to 2019), supplemented by Statistics Denmark with a population survey conducted in November 1970
registers.role: treatment, instrumented variable, and outcomes (maternal and paternal years and levels of education; child education at age 20)

registers.name_in_paper: income information obtained from tax authorities (pre-tax annual labor income including income as self-employed, and disposable income)
registers.role: outcomes (maternal labor income and disposable income)

registers.name_in_paper: register information on employment and unemployment (those with positive labor income are registered as being employed; labor force participation is measured by registered employment or unemployment)
registers.role: outcomes (maternal labor force participation and employment)

registers.name_in_paper: a fertility database, where information on birth weight is recorded from 1977 to 2018
registers.role: outcomes (low and very low birth weight) and fertility measures

registers.name_in_paper: utilization of public health care: inpatient hospitalizations (with diagnoses)
registers.role: outcomes (child and maternal hospitalizations, diagnosis-specific hospitalizations)

registers.name_in_paper: utilization of public health care: services from general practice (meetings, prescriptions, tests, etc.) and services from a psychologist or psychiatrist
registers.role: outcomes (child and maternal general practice use; mental health services)

linkages: Different registers are linked on an individual level because each citizen in Denmark has a unique identification number in the Central Person Registry.

Children are linked to their mothers (and, where available, to their fathers); information on fathers is missing for 16% of the children because they do not appear in the administrative data from 1980 or later.

sample.universe: Children whose mother was born in Denmark between August 1953 and July 1960 and where the mother was between age 13 and 39 when her first child was born; a supplementary sample of all women born in Denmark in the same cohorts is used for the extensive fertility margin.
sample.unit_of_observation: child (cross-section at a given child age) for child outcomes and for the maternal education first stage; mother for maternal health and fertility outcomes; mother-year for maternal labor market outcomes
selection_rules: mother born in Denmark between August 1953 and July 1960
mother aged 13-39 when her first child was born, so that children can be followed to a given age throughout all included maternal cohorts
children in the resulting sample are born between 1968 and 1999; the youngest are 20 years of age in 2019
the 12 monthly maternal cohorts born August 1956 - July 1957 (the donut) are excluded because a large share has missing education data
missing maternal education is imputed as the highest possible level in 1973, i.e. age in 1973 minus 7
for maternal hospitalizations and general practice contacts, those related to pregnancy are excluded
for the 'Employed if in Labor force' outcome, the sample is restricted to mother-years in the labor force
for 'Parental years of education' the sample is restricted to children with paternal information
sample.n_observations: 445,301 children before the donut exclusion (190,494 control, 63,688 donut, 191,119 treated); 381,613 children in the main donut-excluded estimation sample

construction_notes: Low birth weight is defined as birth weight below 2500 g; a lower threshold of 2000 g is used for 'very low birth weight'. Birth weight was reported in 500-gram intervals before 1979 and in 10-gram intervals after that.
The data contain too few children with birth weight below 1,500 or 1,000 grams to use the standard indicators of very low or extremely low birth weight.

Hospitalizations are the number of annual inpatient hospitalizations, excluding those related to pregnancies; general practice use is the number of annual services from general practice (meetings, prescriptions, tests, etc.).
Four broad diagnosis groups are examined for children: gastrointestinal diseases, musculoskeletal diseases, otorhinolaryngology and concussion; only the first two are tabulated in Table 6.
Income is measured from the mother's age 35 to 55; Table 1 reports annual labor and disposable income in 2015 DKK.
The running variable r counts the number of months a mother is born from the first cohort affected by the reform (August 1957), centred at 0; T = 1(r >= 0).
In 'closed donut' specifications the running variable is increased by 12 for the control group, since the last monthly cohort before the donut hole is born 13 months prior to the reform.
f and g are continuous polynomials (1st or 2nd order) in the running variable, interacted with the treatment indicator; the order is chosen by the root-mean-squared error of Eq. (2).
Each birth month is weighted equally with a rectangular kernel and the bandwidth is fixed to 24 months; mean-squared-error-optimal bandwidths are reported to give similar results.
All models include calendar month of birth fixed effects to account for within-birth-year variation.

Missing maternal education is imputed to the highest level possible in 1973 (age in 1973 minus 7); the share with missing education rises from close to zero to 6-8% for cohorts born after November 1956.

claims.statement: The 1972 Danish compulsory schooling reform raised maternal years of education (specification: 1st order polynomial in maternal month of birth, specific to treated and controls, open donut hole (the pre-reform trend is extrapolated through the donut hole), education not imputed).

treatment.label: school reform exposure T = 1(r >= 0) (maternal cohorts born from August 1957)

definition.value: A treatment indicator T taking value one for maternal birth cohorts affected by the 1972 compulsory schooling reform, i.e. mothers born from August 1957 onwards, and zero otherwise (T = 1(r >= 0)). The reform raised compulsory schooling from 7 to 9 years and applied to the cohorts who enrolled in 7th grade by August 1972.

timing.value: maternal birth cohort; exposure is fixed at the mother's birth and the reform bound when she was in 7th grade in 1972

register_source.value: administrative data on schooling and education (completed education from October 1973; ongoing education registered each October 1981-2019), supplemented by Statistics Denmark with the November 1970 population survey

definition.value: Years of completed education for the mother. Missing education is imputed in the specifications marked 'Education imputed: YES': the imputation sets education to be the highest possible level in 1973, assuming it is equal to their age in 1973 minus 7, the school starting age.

timing.value: maternal completed educational attainment, recorded in the administrative education registers from October 1973 onwards

units.value: years of maternal education

estimand.target_population: mothers (and their children) whose month of birth lies close to the August 1957 reform cut-off, within the August 1953-July 1960 maternal birth cohorts
estimand.time_horizon: maternal completed education; no post-treatment horizon is stated
estimand.formal_query: E[Y | do(T = 1)] - E[Y | do(T = 0)] for maternal birth cohorts at the August 1957 reform cut-off

population.description: Children born 1968-1999 whose mother was born in Denmark between August 1953 and July 1960 and who was between age 13 and 39 when her first child was born; the 12 monthly maternal cohorts born August 1956-July 1957 (the donut) are excluded.
population.birth_cohorts: children born 1968-1999; mothers born in Denmark August 1953-July 1960 (donut cohorts August 1956-July 1957 excluded)
population.ages: maternal completed educational attainment, recorded in the administrative education registers from October 1973 onwards
population.selection: Sample restricted to mothers born in Denmark August 1953-July 1960 and aged 13-39 at first birth, so that children can be followed to a given age across all maternal cohorts; the 12 donut cohorts August 1956-July 1957 are dropped because education data are disproportionately missing for them. The dependent variable is the mother's education, but the estimation sample is at the child level: N counts children.

identification.source_of_variation: The Danish compulsory schooling reform of 1972 (Consolidated Act No. 106 of February 3rd, 1972), which raised compulsory schooling from 7 to 9 years for cohorts enrolling in 7th grade by August 1972, i.e. persons born from August 1st 1957 onwards; the running variable is the mother's month of birth relative to that cut-off.

key_assumptions.assumption: Regression-discontinuity continuity: absent the reform, mean outcomes would have evolved continuously in the mother's month of birth across the August 1957 cut-off, once treated- and control-specific polynomial trends f(r), g(r) and calendar month-of-birth fixed effects are included.
key_assumptions.supported_by: RD plots of cohort means against the maternal birth month (Figs. 1-4 and Appendix Figs. A.1-A.13), and sensitivity of the estimates to 1st vs 2nd order polynomials, open vs closed donut, and a non-parametric local linear specification.

formal.as_written: 𝐻𝑐 = 𝛼 + 𝛽𝐸𝑝 + 𝑔 (𝑟) + 𝛾𝑚 + 𝜀𝑐

key_assumptions.assumption: No manipulation of the running variable: a mother's month of birth, and hence her exposure to the reform, could not be chosen, since the reform was proposed and passed in 1972, about fifteen years after the affected cohorts were born.
Nothing other than the reform changes discontinuously at the cut-off: no other cohort-specific shock hits Maternal years of education at the August 1957 maternal birth-cohort threshold.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state the 1972 act was the only school-law change in 1972-1974, that curriculum was unchanged until the separate 1975 reform, and that cohorts on either side entered similar labour markets.

implies_edges.from: other contemporaneous cohort-specific shocks at the August 1957 cut-off

key_assumptions.assumption: The 12 monthly maternal cohorts born August 1956-July 1957 are excluded from the estimation sample, so every estimate is conditioned on the mother not belonging to that donut window.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Appendix Fig. A.1: the share of observations with missing education information rises from close to zero to 6-8% for cohorts born after November 1956.

implies_edges.from: maternal birth cohort in the donut window (August 1956-July 1957)

key_assumptions.assumption: Education imputation: missing maternal education is set to the highest level possible in 1973 (age in 1973 minus 7), which the authors argue is conservative because education is missing primarily for those with low education and missingness is higher just around and after the reform.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors show that dropping missing observations instead overestimates the reform effect (Table 2, columns 1 vs 3).

threats_discussed: missing education data just around and after the reform, which would overestimate the reform effect if missing values were simply dropped
whether the donut hole is left open or closed, which changes how the pre-reform trend is extrapolated
weak-instrument bias, screened with first-stage F-statistics and with the tF-procedure of Lee et al. (2021)
reform-induced changes in fertility and in assortative mating that could confound the child-health estimates
non-random missingness of paternal information
the reform raising education only at the compulsory-schooling margin, so that the estimate is local to a low-education complier group
robustness_checks: 1st vs 2nd order polynomial in the running variable, chosen on the root-mean-squared error
open vs closed donut hole, with the more conservative of the two reported
non-parametric local linear regression with a rectangular kernel and a fixed 24-month bandwidth (Table 2, column 10); mean-squared-error-optimal bandwidths give similar results
education imputed vs observations with missing education dropped
five alternative RD specifications per outcome in Appendix Tables B.2-B.22, with RD plots in Appendix Figs. A.1-A.13
tF-procedure of Lee et al. (2021) applied to the significant maternal-hospitalization estimate
a lower birth-weight threshold of 2000 g alongside the standard 2500 g
unresolved_confounders: the hypothetical scenario where the effects of postponing childbirth precisely counteract the effects of increasing education, which the authors deem unlikely
whether the schooling reform substantially increased paternal education, which a higher fraction of missing data for fathers makes uncertain
parental income as a key mechanism, since the authors do not identify a robust effect of maternal education on labor income

claims.statement: The 1972 Danish compulsory schooling reform raised maternal years of education (specification: 1st order polynomial in maternal month of birth, specific to treated and controls, closed donut hole (the running variable is increased by 12 for the control group), education imputed).

treatment.label: school reform exposure T = 1(r >= 0) (maternal cohorts born from August 1957)

definition.value: A treatment indicator T taking value one for maternal birth cohorts affected by the 1972 compulsory schooling reform, i.e. mothers born from August 1957 onwards, and zero otherwise (T = 1(r >= 0)). The reform raised compulsory schooling from 7 to 9 years and applied to the cohorts who enrolled in 7th grade by August 1972.

timing.value: maternal birth cohort; exposure is fixed at the mother's birth and the reform bound when she was in 7th grade in 1972

register_source.value: administrative data on schooling and education (completed education from October 1973; ongoing education registered each October 1981-2019), supplemented by Statistics Denmark with the November 1970 population survey

definition.value: Years of completed education for the mother. Missing education is imputed in the specifications marked 'Education imputed: YES': the imputation sets education to be the highest possible level in 1973, assuming it is equal to their age in 1973 minus 7, the school starting age.

timing.value: maternal completed educational attainment, recorded in the administrative education registers from October 1973 onwards

units.value: years of maternal education

estimand.target_population: mothers (and their children) whose month of birth lies close to the August 1957 reform cut-off, within the August 1953-July 1960 maternal birth cohorts
estimand.time_horizon: maternal completed education; no post-treatment horizon is stated
estimand.formal_query: E[Y | do(T = 1)] - E[Y | do(T = 0)] for maternal birth cohorts at the August 1957 reform cut-off

population.description: Children born 1968-1999 whose mother was born in Denmark between August 1953 and July 1960 and who was between age 13 and 39 when her first child was born; the 12 monthly maternal cohorts born August 1956-July 1957 (the donut) are excluded.
population.birth_cohorts: children born 1968-1999; mothers born in Denmark August 1953-July 1960 (donut cohorts August 1956-July 1957 excluded)
population.ages: maternal completed educational attainment, recorded in the administrative education registers from October 1973 onwards
population.selection: Sample restricted to mothers born in Denmark August 1953-July 1960 and aged 13-39 at first birth, so that children can be followed to a given age across all maternal cohorts; the 12 donut cohorts August 1956-July 1957 are dropped because education data are disproportionately missing for them. The dependent variable is the mother's education, but the estimation sample is at the child level: N counts children.

identification.source_of_variation: The Danish compulsory schooling reform of 1972 (Consolidated Act No. 106 of February 3rd, 1972), which raised compulsory schooling from 7 to 9 years for cohorts enrolling in 7th grade by August 1972, i.e. persons born from August 1st 1957 onwards; the running variable is the mother's month of birth relative to that cut-off.

key_assumptions.assumption: Regression-discontinuity continuity: absent the reform, mean outcomes would have evolved continuously in the mother's month of birth across the August 1957 cut-off, once treated- and control-specific polynomial trends f(r), g(r) and calendar month-of-birth fixed effects are included.
key_assumptions.supported_by: RD plots of cohort means against the maternal birth month (Figs. 1-4 and Appendix Figs. A.1-A.13), and sensitivity of the estimates to 1st vs 2nd order polynomials, open vs closed donut, and a non-parametric local linear specification.

formal.as_written: 𝐻𝑐 = 𝛼 + 𝛽𝐸𝑝 + 𝑔 (𝑟) + 𝛾𝑚 + 𝜀𝑐

key_assumptions.assumption: No manipulation of the running variable: a mother's month of birth, and hence her exposure to the reform, could not be chosen, since the reform was proposed and passed in 1972, about fifteen years after the affected cohorts were born.
Nothing other than the reform changes discontinuously at the cut-off: no other cohort-specific shock hits Maternal years of education at the August 1957 maternal birth-cohort threshold.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state the 1972 act was the only school-law change in 1972-1974, that curriculum was unchanged until the separate 1975 reform, and that cohorts on either side entered similar labour markets.

implies_edges.from: other contemporaneous cohort-specific shocks at the August 1957 cut-off

key_assumptions.assumption: The 12 monthly maternal cohorts born August 1956-July 1957 are excluded from the estimation sample, so every estimate is conditioned on the mother not belonging to that donut window.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Appendix Fig. A.1: the share of observations with missing education information rises from close to zero to 6-8% for cohorts born after November 1956.

implies_edges.from: maternal birth cohort in the donut window (August 1956-July 1957)

key_assumptions.assumption: Education imputation: missing maternal education is set to the highest level possible in 1973 (age in 1973 minus 7), which the authors argue is conservative because education is missing primarily for those with low education and missingness is higher just around and after the reform.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors show that dropping missing observations instead overestimates the reform effect (Table 2, columns 1 vs 3).

threats_discussed: missing education data just around and after the reform, which would overestimate the reform effect if missing values were simply dropped
whether the donut hole is left open or closed, which changes how the pre-reform trend is extrapolated
weak-instrument bias, screened with first-stage F-statistics and with the tF-procedure of Lee et al. (2021)
reform-induced changes in fertility and in assortative mating that could confound the child-health estimates
non-random missingness of paternal information
the reform raising education only at the compulsory-schooling margin, so that the estimate is local to a low-education complier group
robustness_checks: 1st vs 2nd order polynomial in the running variable, chosen on the root-mean-squared error
open vs closed donut hole, with the more conservative of the two reported
non-parametric local linear regression with a rectangular kernel and a fixed 24-month bandwidth (Table 2, column 10); mean-squared-error-optimal bandwidths give similar results
education imputed vs observations with missing education dropped
five alternative RD specifications per outcome in Appendix Tables B.2-B.22, with RD plots in Appendix Figs. A.1-A.13
tF-procedure of Lee et al. (2021) applied to the significant maternal-hospitalization estimate
a lower birth-weight threshold of 2000 g alongside the standard 2500 g
unresolved_confounders: the hypothetical scenario where the effects of postponing childbirth precisely counteract the effects of increasing education, which the authors deem unlikely
whether the schooling reform substantially increased paternal education, which a higher fraction of missing data for fathers makes uncertain
parental income as a key mechanism, since the authors do not identify a robust effect of maternal education on labor income

population.selection: Sample restricted to mothers born in Denmark August 1953-July 1960 and aged 13-39 at first birth, so that children can be followed to a given age across all maternal cohorts; the 12 donut cohorts August 1956-July 1957 are dropped because education data are disproportionately missing for them. The dependent variable is the mother's education, but the estimation sample is at the child level: N counts children.

identification.source_of_variation: The Danish compulsory schooling reform of 1972 (Consolidated Act No. 106 of February 3rd, 1972), which raised compulsory schooling from 7 to 9 years for cohorts enrolling in 7th grade by August 1972, i.e. persons born from August 1st 1957 onwards; the running variable is the mother's month of birth relative to that cut-off.

key_assumptions.assumption: Regression-discontinuity continuity: absent the reform, mean outcomes would have evolved continuously in the mother's month of birth across the August 1957 cut-off, once treated- and control-specific polynomial trends f(r), g(r) and calendar month-of-birth fixed effects are included.
key_assumptions.supported_by: RD plots of cohort means against the maternal birth month (Figs. 1-4 and Appendix Figs. A.1-A.13), and sensitivity of the estimates to 1st vs 2nd order polynomials, open vs closed donut, and a non-parametric local linear specification.

formal.as_written: 𝐻𝑐 = 𝛼 + 𝛽𝐸𝑝 + 𝑔 (𝑟) + 𝛾𝑚 + 𝜀𝑐

key_assumptions.assumption: No manipulation of the running variable: a mother's month of birth, and hence her exposure to the reform, could not be chosen, since the reform was proposed and passed in 1972, about fifteen years after the affected cohorts were born.
Nothing other than the reform changes discontinuously at the cut-off: no other cohort-specific shock hits 9th grade at the August 1957 maternal birth-cohort threshold.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state the 1972 act was the only school-law change in 1972-1974, that curriculum was unchanged until the separate 1975 reform, and that cohorts on either side entered similar labour markets.

implies_edges.from: other contemporaneous cohort-specific shocks at the August 1957 cut-off

key_assumptions.assumption: The 12 monthly maternal cohorts born August 1956-July 1957 are excluded from the estimation sample, so every estimate is conditioned on the mother not belonging to that donut window.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Appendix Fig. A.1: the share of observations with missing education information rises from close to zero to 6-8% for cohorts born after November 1956.

implies_edges.from: maternal birth cohort in the donut window (August 1956-July 1957)

key_assumptions.assumption: Education imputation: missing maternal education is set to the highest level possible in 1973 (age in 1973 minus 7), which the authors argue is conservative because education is missing primarily for those with low education and missingness is higher just around and after the reform.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors show that dropping missing observations instead overestimates the reform effect (Table 2, columns 1 vs 3).

threats_discussed: missing education data just around and after the reform, which would overestimate the reform effect if missing values were simply dropped
whether the donut hole is left open or closed, which changes how the pre-reform trend is extrapolated
weak-instrument bias, screened with first-stage F-statistics and with the tF-procedure of Lee et al. (2021)
reform-induced changes in fertility and in assortative mating that could confound the child-health estimates
non-random missingness of paternal information
the reform raising education only at the compulsory-schooling margin, so that the estimate is local to a low-education complier group
robustness_checks: 1st vs 2nd order polynomial in the running variable, chosen on the root-mean-squared error
open vs closed donut hole, with the more conservative of the two reported
non-parametric local linear regression with a rectangular kernel and a fixed 24-month bandwidth (Table 2, column 10); mean-squared-error-optimal bandwidths give similar results
education imputed vs observations with missing education dropped
five alternative RD specifications per outcome in Appendix Tables B.2-B.22, with RD plots in Appendix Figs. A.1-A.13
tF-procedure of Lee et al. (2021) applied to the significant maternal-hospitalization estimate
a lower birth-weight threshold of 2000 g alongside the standard 2500 g
unresolved_confounders: the hypothetical scenario where the effects of postponing childbirth precisely counteract the effects of increasing education, which the authors deem unlikely

treatment.label: school reform exposure T = 1(r >= 0) (maternal cohorts born from August 1957)

definition.value: A treatment indicator T taking value one for maternal birth cohorts affected by the 1972 compulsory schooling reform, i.e. mothers born from August 1957 onwards, and zero otherwise (T = 1(r >= 0)). The reform raised compulsory schooling from 7 to 9 years and applied to the cohorts who enrolled in 7th grade by August 1972.

timing.value: maternal birth cohort; exposure is fixed at the mother's birth and the reform bound when she was in 7th grade in 1972

definition.value: Indicator of labor force participation, measured by registered employment or unemployment. (The Table 5 note describes column (5) as 'Indicator of employment measured as positive labor income'; the column heading reads 'In Labor force'.)

timing.value: mother-year observations at mother's age 35-55

units.value: share (0-1 scale) of mother-years in the labor force

population.description: Mothers born in Denmark between August 1953 and July 1960 who gave birth to their first child at age 13-39; the 12 monthly cohorts born August 1956-July 1957 (the donut) are excluded.

identification.source_of_variation: The Danish compulsory schooling reform of 1972 (Consolidated Act No. 106 of February 3rd, 1972), which raised compulsory schooling from 7 to 9 years for cohorts enrolling in 7th grade by August 1972, i.e. persons born from August 1st 1957 onwards; the running variable is the mother's month of birth relative to that cut-off.

key_assumptions.supported_by: RD plots of cohort means against the maternal birth month (Figs. 1-4 and Appendix Figs. A.1-A.13), and sensitivity of the estimates to 1st vs 2nd order polynomials, open vs closed donut, and a non-parametric local linear specification.

definition.value: Years of completed education for the mother. Missing education is imputed in the specifications marked 'Education imputed: YES': the imputation sets education to be the highest possible level in 1973, assuming it is equal to their age in 1973 minus 7, the school starting age.

timing.value: maternal completed educational attainment, recorded in the administrative education registers from October 1973 onwards

estimand.compliers: the children of parents who went to school immediately after the school reform was implemented and would have dropped out of school after 7 years in the absence of the reform
estimand.formal_query: E[Y | do(E_p = e+1)] - E[Y | do(E_p = e)] for compliers at the August 1957 reform cut-off

population.description: Mothers born in Denmark between August 1953 and July 1960 who gave birth to their first child at age 13-39; the 12 monthly cohorts born August 1956-July 1957 (the donut) are excluded.
population.birth_cohorts: mothers born in Denmark August 1953-July 1960 (donut cohorts August 1956-July 1957 excluded)
population.selection: Sample restricted to mothers born in Denmark August 1953-July 1960 and aged 13-39 at first birth, so that children can be followed to a given age across all maternal cohorts; the 12 donut cohorts August 1956-July 1957 are dropped because education data are disproportionately missing for them. General practice data are available from 1990 onwards.

identification.source_of_variation: The Danish compulsory schooling reform of 1972 (Consolidated Act No. 106 of February 3rd, 1972), which raised compulsory schooling from 7 to 9 years for persons born from August 1st 1957 onwards, used as an instrument for maternal years of education; the running variable is the mother's month of birth relative to that cut-off.
identification.instrument: The school reform dummy T = 1(r >= 0), equal to one for maternal cohorts born from August 1957 who were subject to 9 rather than 7 years of compulsory schooling, used as an instrument for maternal years of education in a fuzzy regression discontinuity design.

key_assumptions.assumption: Instrument relevance: the 1972 compulsory schooling reform shifted maternal years of education discontinuously at the August 1957 cut-off, giving a non-zero first stage.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 2 first-stage estimates (0.125 to 0.353 additional years, all starred at p<0.01) and the reported first-stage F-statistics, which the authors read as rejecting a weak instrument in the spirit of Stock and Yogo (2005).

implies_edges.from: school reform exposure T = 1(r >= 0) (maternal cohorts born from August 1957)

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion restriction: being in a cohort subject to the reform affects General practice use, Age 54-58 (mother) only through maternal years of education.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors argue the reform was implemented independently of other changes (e.g. curriculum), that no simultaneous school-law changes occurred in 1972-1974, that peer composition and school resources were essentially unchanged, and that cohorts on either side entered similar labour markets.

implies_edges.from: school reform exposure T = 1(r >= 0) (maternal cohorts born from August 1957)

key_assumptions.supported_by: RD plots of cohort means against the maternal birth month (Figs. 1-4 and Appendix Figs. A.1-A.13), and sensitivity of the estimates to 1st vs 2nd order polynomials, open vs closed donut, and a non-parametric local linear specification.

key_assumptions.assumption: No manipulation of the running variable: a mother's month of birth, and hence her exposure to the reform, could not be chosen, since the reform was proposed and passed in 1972, about fifteen years after the affected cohorts were born.

Monotonicity / no defiers, so that the 2SLS coefficient is a local average treatment effect for compliers: the children of parents who went to school immediately after the reform and would have dropped out after 7 years in its absence.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors invoke Imbens and Angrist (1994) and name the complier group explicitly.

key_assumptions.assumption: The 12 monthly maternal cohorts born August 1956-July 1957 are excluded from the estimation sample, so every estimate is conditioned on the mother not belonging to that donut window.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Appendix Fig. A.1: the share of observations with missing education information rises from close to zero to 6-8% for cohorts born after November 1956.

implies_edges.from: maternal birth cohort in the donut window (August 1956-July 1957)

key_assumptions.assumption: Education imputation: missing maternal education is set to the highest level possible in 1973 (age in 1973 minus 7), which the authors argue is conservative because education is missing primarily for those with low education and missingness is higher just around and after the reform.

implies_edges.from: school reform exposure T = 1(r >= 0) (maternal cohorts born from August 1957)

key_assumptions.assumption: Regression-discontinuity continuity: absent the reform, mean outcomes would have evolved continuously in the mother's month of birth across the August 1957 cut-off, once treated- and control-specific polynomial trends f(r), g(r) and calendar month-of-birth fixed effects are included.
key_assumptions.supported_by: RD plots of cohort means against the maternal birth month (Figs. 1-4 and Appendix Figs. A.1-A.13), and sensitivity of the estimates to 1st vs 2nd order polynomials, open vs closed donut, and a non-parametric local linear specification.

key_assumptions.assumption: No manipulation of the running variable: a mother's month of birth, and hence her exposure to the reform, could not be chosen, since the reform was proposed and passed in 1972, about fifteen years after the affected cohorts were born.

Monotonicity / no defiers, so that the 2SLS coefficient is a local average treatment effect for compliers: the children of parents who went to school immediately after the reform and would have dropped out after 7 years in its absence.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors invoke Imbens and Angrist (1994) and name the complier group explicitly.

key_assumptions.assumption: The 12 monthly maternal cohorts born August 1956-July 1957 are excluded from the estimation sample, so every estimate is conditioned on the mother not belonging to that donut window.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Appendix Fig. A.1: the share of observations with missing education information rises from close to zero to 6-8% for cohorts born after November 1956.

implies_edges.from: maternal birth cohort in the donut window (August 1956-July 1957)

key_assumptions.assumption: Education imputation: missing maternal education is set to the highest level possible in 1973 (age in 1973 minus 7), which the authors argue is conservative because education is missing primarily for those with low education and missingness is higher just around and after the reform.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors show that dropping missing observations instead overestimates the reform effect (Table 2, columns 1 vs 3).

whether the donut hole is left open or closed, which changes how the pre-reform trend is extrapolated
weak-instrument bias, screened with first-stage F-statistics and with the tF-procedure of Lee et al. (2021)
reform-induced changes in fertility and in assortative mating that could confound the child-health estimates
non-random missingness of paternal information
the reform raising education only at the compulsory-schooling margin, so that the estimate is local to a low-education complier group
robustness_checks: 1st vs 2nd order polynomial in the running variable, chosen on the root-mean-squared error
open vs closed donut hole, with the more conservative of the two reported
non-parametric local linear regression with a rectangular kernel and a fixed 24-month bandwidth (Table 2, column 10); mean-squared-error-optimal bandwidths give similar results
education imputed vs observations with missing education dropped
five alternative RD specifications per outcome in Appendix Tables B.2-B.22, with RD plots in Appendix Figs. A.1-A.13
tF-procedure of Lee et al. (2021) applied to the significant maternal-hospitalization estimate
a lower birth-weight threshold of 2000 g alongside the standard 2500 g

whether the schooling reform substantially increased paternal education, which a higher fraction of missing data for fathers makes uncertain
parental income as a key mechanism, since the authors do not identify a robust effect of maternal education on labor income

value.normalisation: T = 1(r >= 0); the running variable r counts the number of months a mother is born from the first cohort affected by the reform (August 1957), centred at 0. The 12 donut cohorts born 1956:8-1957:7 are excluded; this column uses a 1st order polynomial in maternal month of birth, specific to treated and controls and closed donut hole (the running variable is increased by 12 for the control group). f and g are continuous functions of the running variable interacted with the treatment indicator. E_p is instrumented by T, the first stage being Eq. (1); the resulting 2SLS coefficient is a local average treatment effect rather than a constant effect.
value.link_function: identity; a linear probability model when the dependent variable is a 0/1 indicator

value.claimed_domain: Denmark in the current context; the authors hedge that the null may be specific to a highly egalitarian country with a compressed earnings distribution and a large universal welfare state, and that the estimate is local to the compulsory-schooling margin
boundary_conditions: the reform mainly increases education at the lower end of the distribution, so nothing is claimed about marginal increases at higher education levels
the estimate is a local average treatment effect for compliers who would have completed only seven years of education absent the reform
results concern maternal, not paternal, education
